steps.what: List stored reading and conference rows
Read current programming practices
Attend professional conferences or workshops
Sign the learning note
File the signed learning note
outputs: filed copy of signed learning note v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored reading and conference rows in {LMS}. The developer reads current programming practices and attends the conferences or workshops. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}. The job does not summarise the reading.
tasks.previous_blocker: Course titles were recopied before each reading.
tasks.enabler_now: Course identifier and title are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding still comes from the reading and the room.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides what is worth keeping.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week reading and attending, not on assembling the list.

evidence.claim: Digest [S4] says a coding draft needs oversight. The developer still reviews the change.

assumptions: Course identifier, title, and date are stored on the learning record. The learning record produces them. A blank title stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the learning record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining reading time is still the developer reading the practices.

incremental.description: Refresh course identifier and title when the learning layout changes, and drop a list the developer has not opened.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many course titles are blank. The high end assumes course identifier and title are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List request rows with a blank requirement
Analyze user needs on those requests
Determine the technical requirements
Sign the requirement note
File the signed requirement note
outputs: filed copy of signed requirement note v1

tasks.design: A job lists request rows with a blank requirement in {HELPDESK}. The developer analyzes the user needs and determines the technical requirements. A later job files the signed note in {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests were copied into a fresh pack before the analysis.
tasks.enabler_now: Request identifier and the requirement field are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The need is still heard from the user.

ambition.what: Set the requirement the week the request is stored.

tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the requirement, not on collecting requests.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a pipeline tests and scans every change, work stays on a branch, and a person merges.

assumptions: Request identifier, user need, and requirement field are stored on the request record. The request record produces them. A blank requirement stays blank until the developer writes it.
Native configuration of the request record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining analysis time is still the developer analyzing the needs.

incremental.description: Refresh request identifier and requirement field when the request layout changes, and drop a note the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many requirement fields are blank. The high end assumes request identifier and requirement field are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Match email inquiries to stored responses
Respond when no stored response matches
Set the automated system to that response
Sign the email response
Send only the signed email response
outputs: filed copy of signed email response v1

tasks.design: A job matches email inquiries to stored responses in {EMAIL}. The developer writes the response when no row matches, and sets the automated system to that signed text. A later job sends only the signed response. No model writes the reply.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers were searched by hand before each reply.
tasks.enabler_now: Inquiry type and response text are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: A new question still needs the developer.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides the response text.
tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on unmatched inquiries, not on finding a stored response.

evidence.claim: Digest [S4] says a coding draft needs oversight. The developer still reviews the change.

assumptions: Inquiry type, response text, and response identifier are stored on the answer record. The answer record produces them. If no row matches, the list shows no match and the developer writes the response.
Native configuration of the answer record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
The automated send uses only the signed response text. It does not invent a reply.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining reply time is still the developer writing the response.

incremental.description: Refresh inquiry type and response text when the mail layout changes, and drop a response the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many inquiries have no stored response. The high end assumes inquiry type and response text are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List domain registrations due by interval
Decide which domain registration to renew
Check the fee before any payment
Sign the domain renewal
Send only the signed renewal request
outputs: filed copy of signed renewal request v1

tasks.design: A job lists domain registrations that are due by the stored expiry and renewal interval in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The developer decides which registration to renew and checks the fee. A later job sends only that signed request by {EMAIL}. It does not pay.
tasks.previous_blocker: Expiry dates were copied onto a sheet before the decision.
tasks.enabler_now: Expiry date and renewal interval are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The fee and the decision stay with the developer.
tasks.human_edge: The developer decides whether to renew.

ambition.what: Renew a domain in the week the interval marks it due.

tasks.altitude: The developer spends the week on the renewal decision, not on finding due names.

reach.task: Act only on the signed request

evidence.claim: The executive digest says a pipeline tests and scans every change, work stays on a branch, and a person merges.

assumptions: Domain name, expiry date, renewal interval, and fee are stored on the registrar record. The registrar record produces them. A registration is due when the expiry date falls inside the renewal interval measured from today. A blank expiry or a blank interval is shown as not due.
Native configuration of the registrar record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the developer signed is filed or sent.
The send is the signed request. It is not a payment.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining decision time is still the developer deciding the renewal.

incremental.description: Refresh expiry date and renewal interval when the registrar layout changes, and drop a request the developer has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes expiry or interval is often blank. The high end assumes expiry date and renewal interval are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The web developer spends the week writing, reviewing, and merging. A stored failing check, a blank field, and filing a signed note can move. The developer still reviews every change, and no job changes a live system alone.
reach: A reviewer reads the change before the developer merges it.
A specialist receives only the notice the developer signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a list that is missing a stored field.
Reject a sentence that does not restate a stored row.
Reject a live change that is not the signed set.
role.ambitious_version: A signed change can be filed the same week, and the developer still owns the merge.
